response: The use of cyanoacrylate, specifically ethyl-2-cyanoacrylate, in intestinal anastomosis has shown promising results as a reliable alternative to traditional sutures. In experimental settings, it has been found to achieve better healing, shorter anastomosis time, and equal strength compared to polyglactin 910 sutures. This suggests that cyanoacrylate could be a viable option for intestinal anastomosis, offering potential benefits in terms of healing and procedure time. However, further research and clinical trials may be necessary to fully establish its efficacy and safety in human patients.
